To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integration of humans and algorithms in solving matching problems is beneficial and that this integration is a function of the problem and the data.

1) humans are better at matching when they have access to a small number of examples; 2) humans can be better than machines when they have access only to training data; 3) humans can be worse than machines when they can access both training and test data.

the human and machine collaboration in solving matching problems can be more effective if humans are allowed to focus on the more complex aspects of the task.
the human-machine integration in matching problems is not only possible, but it is also necessary.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
humans and machines are equally important and complementary to each other in the process of solving matching problems.
humans and machines have complementary roles in achieving a cognitive task.
the role of the human in matching is to provide the algorithm with the right data, and the algorithm will then do the heavy lifting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
humans and machines can be successfully integrated in solving matching tasks.
humans and machines can be integrated in a synergistic way to solve matching problems, where humans are in the loop, but not necessarily on the loop.
the roles of humans and algorithms are not static, and they can be dynamically adjusted depending on the data, the task, and the available computational resources.
